findings.location: Baseline Part A §4 Proposition 2 and §7 Result A
findings.summary: Single-experiment marginal equivalence does not imply equality of repeated/joint observation laws.
findings.repair: Restrict to one non-adaptive run or use protocol-level equivalence.

findings.summary: Minimum/maximum formulations require attainment; a continuation infimum may not be attained.
findings.repair: Use infimum/supremum and state attainment separately.

findings.summary: Expected-loss stopping logic cannot be transferred to robust criteria without separate definitions and proof.
findings.repair: Separate robust objective, uncertainty set, policy class, update rule, and dynamic assumptions.

findings.summary: EVSI nonnegativity needs well-defined risks, posterior, measurability and integrability/extended-real conventions.
findings.repair: Use v3.2 §5.1 assumptions.

findings.summary: Measurability of h↦P_h^e(B) and h↦Law_h^π(B) is needed to construct joint/prior-predictive laws and posteriors.
findings.repair: Specify Markov kernels and standard-Borel or equivalent posterior-existence conditions.

findings.summary: Protocol equivalence does not cover an arbitrary policy unless every admissible policy induces a protocol in Π.
findings.repair: Add policy-to-protocol condition and h-independent measurable terminal decision rule.

findings.summary: Equal likelihood of a past history preserves posterior odds but not future kernels or continuation values; root proof alone is insufficient.
findings.repair: Require conditional protocol equivalence after the history and prove a conditional result, or remove the broad claim.

findings.summary: Equality between integrated pointwise posterior infimum and infimum over measurable decision rules needs measurable-selection/epsilon-optimality conditions.
findings.repair: Define post-experiment risk via measurable decision rules or state conditions ensuring equality.

findings.summary: Pure stop/continue classes do not partition a universe that admits randomized mixtures; for expected loss mixtures cannot improve below the smaller class infimum.
findings.repair: Define pure D_stop/D_cont, global Δ and mixture convention explicitly.

findings.summary: Standard-Borel conditions should identify the conditioned hypothesis space and observation space, not just say 'common setting'.
findings.repair: Require H standard Borel and D_e standard Borel, or equivalent regular-conditional-distribution conditions.

findings.summary: R_e may be −∞ under an extended-real loss convention, so EVSI may be +∞ rather than a finite difference.
findings.repair: Require R_e>−∞ for finite EVSI or explicitly allow extended-real EVSI.

findings.summary: The comparison is root-level; sequential implementation needs Bellman and measurable-selection conditions, and degenerate empty/infinite cases need scope.
findings.repair: Label root-level rule and state dynamic-programming assumptions for sequential use.

findings.summary: A positive minimum cost plus finite budget ensures finite termination only with a hard pathwise budget and suitable deterministic/almost-sure cost bound.
findings.repair: State cost and budget conventions explicitly.

findings.summary: The sequence decreases to 1/3 without attaining it at finite n; non-attainment depends on finite termination and the allowed experiment sequence.
findings.repair: Give the θ∼Uniform[0,1) bit-revelation realization and restrict to sequential prefix queries.

findings.summary: The example gives ex-ante versus conditionally re-optimized value discrepancy for pure actions, not a plan reversal or stop/continue counterexample.
findings.repair: Describe as failure of the specified value recursion and define prior-by-prior conditional re-optimization.

findings.summary: For an exact union of pure policy classes inf F equals the minimum of class infima; mixture-admissible robust classes can do better due to convexity.
findings.repair: Correct the union identity and explain the mixture effect.

findings.summary: Kernel-equality condition needs induction by history length, positive-probability reachability for counterexamples, and non-anticipating consistency.
findings.repair: State induction, reachability and non-anticipation explicitly.

findings.summary: Equal history laws imply LR=1 almost surely; posterior-odds equality additionally requires positive prior masses and predictive support.
findings.repair: State μ(h)>0 and μ(h')>0 and almost-sure scope.

findings.summary: Robust invariance over a set of priors is not defined by a single-prior mass move; a vague 'relevant' sentence is not a theorem.
findings.repair: Define a transformation on the prior set or remove the claim.

findings.summary: Single-experiment equivalence plus loss equivalence does not preserve EVSI under repeated performance; reported values are 1/2 and 1/4.
findings.repair: Optional explanatory remark.

findings.summary: Notation overload (π prior/protocol), Proposition 1b numbering, and redundant cost condition create avoidable ambiguity.
findings.repair: Unify notation and proposition labels; remove genuinely redundant condition only after checking the cost model.

priority_repairs: Connect every admissible policy to protocol class Π; remove unsupported same-likelihood continuation claim.
Specify measurable decision rules/selection conditions for posterior-risk representation.
Separate pure stopping/continuation classes from mixture-admissible global class.
Clarify robust value recursion and mixtures.
State hard budget/cost conditions and finite-termination restriction for non-attainment example.
Mark baseline claims as superseded by the proposal where applicable.
claims_not_established: Physical validity or empirical support of OMEGA-ISOP
Sequential optimality of the stopping rule without dynamic-programming assumptions
Canonical acceptance, CE-V promotion, or RL registration
limitations: The report states calculations were done by hand without external tools, code or sources.
Standard measure-theoretic results were assumed by reference rather than reproved.
The review is not evidence of physical or empirical validity.
